title: FreeMate Beginner Chess Course
description: A structured path from rules and piece movement through openings, blunder checks, and basic tactics.

categories.title: Rules of the Game
categories.description: Learn how the board works, how turns work, and how a chess game ends.

lessons.title: Name Every Square
lessons.summary: Use files and ranks to identify squares like d4, e5, and h8.
lessons.coachIntro: A chess coach always starts with the map. If you can name squares, every later lesson becomes easier.

steps.title: Think of the board like a map
steps.body: Files are the lettered columns. They help you find a square from left to right.

steps.title: Find the d-file
steps.body: Click every square on the d-file.
steps.successText: Nice. You found the entire d-file.

steps.title: Find rank 4
steps.body: Now click every square on rank 4.

steps.title: Find d4
steps.body: Click the square where file d and rank 4 meet.
steps.successText: Great. d4 is the intersection of the d-file and rank 4.

exercise.prompt: Finish by clicking d4 one more time.

lessons.title: Checkmate vs Stalemate
lessons.summary: Understand the difference between a forced win and a drawn position.
lessons.coachIntro: Beginners often mix up checkmate and stalemate. This lesson gives you a simple ending checklist.

steps.title: A king under attack is in check
steps.body: The board shows a simple check position. Notice which squares matter around the king.

steps.title: See the safe squares
steps.body: Click the only safe square or move that keeps the king alive.
steps.successText: Good. You recognized the safe idea in the position.

steps.title: Checkmate means no escape
steps.body: A checkmate position leaves the king attacked with no safe square and no block or capture.

steps.title: Spot stalemate clues
steps.body: In stalemate, the king is not in check, but has no legal move.

tasks: Does the king have a legal move?
Can another piece block or capture?

categories.title: Piece Movement
categories.description: Practice how each piece moves and captures.

lessons.title: Move the Rook from d4
lessons.summary: Move the rook horizontally or vertically and avoid diagonal moves.
lessons.coachIntro: Rooks are powerful because they control long straight lines. You will see the legal squares, move the rook, then capture a target.

steps.title: Rooks travel on ranks and files
steps.body: A rook moves in straight lines only.

steps.title: Try a rook move
steps.body: Move the rook to any highlighted square from d4.
steps.successText: Nice. That is how a rook travels across a rank or file.

steps.title: Capture the hanging pawn
steps.body: Now capture the loose pawn on d7. The rook must move straight up the d-file.
steps.successText: Excellent. You used the rook's file to capture the hanging pawn.

exercise.prompt: Choose a destination square for the rook. The backend validates the move with python-chess.

lessons.title: Bishop Movement
lessons.summary: Learn how bishops travel diagonally and stay on one color.
lessons.coachIntro: Bishops and knights are both minor pieces, but their movement shapes are completely different.

steps.title: Bishops stay on diagonals
steps.body: Watch the diagonal lanes radiating from the bishop.

steps.title: Move the bishop
steps.body: Pick any highlighted diagonal square.

steps.title: See a diagonal capture
steps.body: Bishops capture the same way they move. Try spotting the capture line before you click.

exercise.prompt: Move the bishop along one more diagonal square.

lessons.title: Knight Movement
lessons.coachIntro: Knights feel strange at first because they are the only pieces that jump.

steps.title: Knights jump in an L
steps.body: The highlighted squares show every legal knight landing square.

steps.title: Jump the knight
steps.body: Drag the knight to any highlighted landing square.
steps.successText: Nice. Knights really do jump like that.

steps.title: Knight capture idea
steps.body: Notice how a knight can fork two pieces at once.

exercise.prompt: Make one more legal knight jump.

lessons.title: Queen Movement
lessons.summary: Combine rook lines and bishop diagonals.
lessons.coachIntro: The queen is powerful because she combines straight and diagonal movement.

steps.title: Queen combines two patterns
steps.body: The queen can move like a rook and a bishop.

steps.title: Test a queen move
steps.body: Move the queen to any legal straight or diagonal square.
steps.successText: Correct. The queen combines both movement patterns.

steps.title: Queen attack lines
steps.body: See both the diagonal and straight lines from the queen.

lessons.title: King Movement
lessons.summary: Move the king safely one square at a time.
lessons.coachIntro: The king is slow, but every move matters because the king can never move into check.

steps.title: Kings move one square
steps.body: The king can move one square in any direction.

steps.title: Move the king safely
steps.body: Choose a safe adjacent square for the king.
steps.successText: Good. The king moved one square and stayed safe.

steps.title: Illegal king moves
steps.body: A king can never move into check, even if the square looks empty.

exercise.prompt: Find one more safe king move.

lessons.title: Pawn Movement
lessons.summary: Learn pawn moves, captures, first moves, and promotion.
lessons.coachIntro: Pawns look simple, but their movement rules create many beginner mistakes.

steps.title: Pawns move forward
steps.body: White pawns go up the board. Black pawns go down.

steps.title: Try a pawn move
steps.body: Move the pawn one or two squares forward if the path is clear.
steps.successText: Good. Pawns move forward like that.

steps.title: Pawn captures diagonally
steps.body: Pawns capture on the diagonals, not straight ahead.

steps.title: Promotion idea
steps.body: A pawn that reaches the last rank becomes a new piece.

exercise.prompt: Make one more legal pawn move.

categories.title: Basic Opening Principles
categories.description: Build good habits in the first few moves of the game.

lessons.title: Choose a Legal First Move
lessons.summary: Practice common first moves that help control the center or develop a piece.
lessons.coachIntro: Openings are easier when you focus on goals instead of memorizing long move lists.

steps.title: The center matters
steps.body: The four center squares are the ones beginners should notice first.

steps.title: Play for the center
steps.body: Try a good first move that helps control the center.
steps.successText: Great. That move helps fight for the center or develop a piece.

steps.title: Develop, then attack
steps.body: After the first move, your next goal is usually to develop another piece.

exercise.prompt: Make a second good opening move from the starting position.

categories.title: Blunder Checks
categories.description: Pause before moving so you do not give away pieces for free.

lessons.title: Checks, Captures, Threats
lessons.summary: Use a quick scan before every move.
lessons.coachIntro: Most beginner games are decided by one-move mistakes. A short safety scan prevents many of them.

steps.title: Checks first
steps.body: Look for forcing moves before you spend time on slow ideas.

steps.title: Spot the forcing move
steps.body: Click the move that most urgently demands a response.
steps.successText: Good. You found the forcing idea.

steps.title: Then captures and threats
steps.body: Loose pieces and hanging kings are where beginners lose material.

steps.title: Spot the danger
steps.body: Find the move that creates the biggest immediate problem for your opponent.

exercise.prompt: Use the checks, captures, threats scan on the board.

categories.title: Basic Tactics
categories.description: Recognize simple patterns that win material or create checkmate threats.

lessons.title: Spot the Fork Idea
lessons.summary: A fork attacks two valuable targets at the same time.
lessons.coachIntro: Tactics are patterns. You do not need magic vision, just a repeatable way to search.

steps.title: A fork hits two targets
steps.body: One piece attacks two valuable pieces at once.

steps.title: Find the fork idea
steps.body: Look for the move that creates two problems at the same time.

steps.title: Test a fork move
steps.body: Move the knight to the square that forks the targets if possible.
steps.successText: Nice. That's the kind of move that creates a fork.

exercise.prompt: Try to make the fork move on the board.
